memory_update.text: PAR is the highest-priority underfollowed public candidate for this node because it owns restaurant-specific POS, Punchh loyalty/customer engagement, PAR Ordering, and PAR Pay assets; next layer should verify ARR mix, retention, customer concentration, and software attach.

Shift4 is a second underfollowed candidate through SkyTab and integrated payments; the key question is whether SkyTab is a real restaurant operating-system wedge or mostly a payment-acquisition funnel.

Toast and DoorDash should be retained as reference leaders for pricing/competition context: Toast anchors restaurant-owned operating systems, while DoorDash anchors aggregator demand and merchant-services expansion.

Olo is highly relevant to direct ordering, delivery enablement, guest-data aggregation, and enterprise restaurant software, but appears no longer US-listed after the 2025 Thoma Bravo acquisition; track only as a private competitor/comparable.

PAR should remain a priority underfollowed candidate for restaurant first-party data infrastructure because its Punchh, PAR Ordering, PAR POS, PAR Pay, and PAR OPS assets map directly to loyalty, ordering, payments, and operational-data control.

Shift4 should remain in the second-order underfollowed lane as a restaurant/hospitality payments and POS-integration provider, but its thesis needs evidence on restaurant-specific mix and Shift4 Dine/SkyTab adoption.

DoorDash is the reference benchmark for marketplace-driven demand aggregation; Toast is the reference benchmark for restaurant-owned operating system rails; smaller candidates should be assessed against these two poles.
Olo would have been one of the cleanest public pure plays for white-label direct ordering and guest data, but it is no longer suitable for the US-listed universe after its acquisition and delisting.

Need a follow-up pass on speculative shadow names in restaurant voice ordering, AI phone agents, gift-card processors, franchise CRM, and customer-data platforms; SoundHound AI surfaced as a possible but high-attention and less pure candidate requiring stricter revenue-mix verification.
PAR is a high-relevance underfollowed candidate for the restaurant first-party data node because Punchh/Ordering/MENU directly map to loyalty, ordering, guest data, and omnichannel engagement.

NCR Voyix is a low-attention restaurant-commerce infrastructure candidate; its post-spin complexity and mixed retail/restaurant label may hide restaurant POS, ordering, loyalty, payment, and white-label app exposure.

SoundHound AI belongs in the speculative-shadow lane: restaurant voice ordering could be a direct-order capture chokepoint, but revenue durability, deployment economics, and switching costs require verification.
Olo’s 2025 take-private removed the cleanest listed restaurant digital-ordering pure play, so remaining public exposure is more indirect through POS, payments, loyalty suites, and AI-ordering layers.

For this node, the key falsification tests are: weak restaurant SaaS retention, low module attach rates, limited evidence that brands migrate order volume to first-party channels, or aggregator partnerships becoming the dominant growth driver rather than owned-channel software.
For the restaurant customer-relationship chokepoint, prioritize PAR and VYX as underfollowed small-cap software/POS rails that map directly to loyalty, ordering, payments, and first-party data.

DoorDash should remain the reference aggregator anchor, but the alpha-hunt lane should focus on infrastructure vendors that let restaurants keep demand generation, customer identity, payment data, and dispatch orchestration closer to first-party channels.

Olo would have been one of the cleanest public-market mappings for this node, but current evidence suggests it was acquired by Thoma Bravo in 2025. Re-verify listing status before including in any public-company universe.

Need later-layer verification of customer concentration, net revenue retention, module attach rates, and actual restaurant revenue mix for PAR, VYX, and FOUR before treating them as durable chokepoint beneficiaries.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around the restaurant digital-demand-control chokepoint. The obvious reference lane is DoorDash as the high-scale delivery marketplace and Toast as the scaled restaurant operating/payment platform. The underfollowed lane is more interesting for this node: PAR Technology and Shift4 both sell restaurant-specific POS, loyalty, ordering, marketing, payments, and data rails that can help restaurants preserve first-party demand and reduce dependence on aggregator-only traffic. Olo would have been a highly relevant pure-play, but evidence indicates it was taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2025, so it is recorded as a coverage gap rather than an active US-listed candidate. Expanded the public-market universe for the restaurant digital-demand-control node. The cleanest reference anchor is DoorDash because it controls marketplace traffic, delivery dispatch, membership frequency, and merchant commerce tools. Toast is a large but unusually pure restaurant operating-system reference name. The underfollowed lane is better represented by PAR Technology and Shift4: both sit one step away from the consumer-facing delivery debate and monetize restaurant ordering, POS, loyalty, payments, and operational data rails. Olo would have been a strong historical candidate for white-label ordering, but it is excluded from the candidate list because external evidence indicates its common stock ceased trading after the Thoma Bravo acquisition.
